categories: what the concept IS, from MRSTY semantic types grouped by robustehr.categories. A concept carrying several types lands in several categories, so category counts SUM TO MORE than the set size. `uncategorised` maps to none of the twelve.

exclusive_partition.lab_measurement_is_not_a_column: lab_measurement is the union T034 (lab_result) and T059 (a procedure), because it deliberately spans both readings of an analyte like `Hgb-9.9`. With procedure and lab_result both present it has no exclusive territory, so listing it would report a structural zero as a measurement. `lab_measurement_union` carries the total instead.
exclusive_partition.other: in none of the eight — organisms, non-drug chemicals, qualifiers
exclusive_partition.rule: a concept is counted under the FIRST category in this order it matches, so the columns sum to the set size. The shipped taxonomy is a lattice — disorder is the parent of disease, symptom and finding — which is right for targeting and wrong for a table a reader sums.

facets: how the concept got in: disorder = descendant closure, medication = MED-RT may_treat with bounded ancestor lift plus declared seeds, finding = declared seeds expanded by closure (UMLS has no usable disease->symptom relation; see concepts/facets.py)
licence: identifiers and counts only; no UMLS string appears here

question: what is in each phenotype's concept set, by facet and by category?
why_both: facets are checked for coverage gaps, categories for contamination. A disorder facet full of anatomy concepts is a closure that wandered.
